notes:
Inbound self-serve signup (trial) -> signed up 2026-02-22 via GitHub OAuth. Small engineering team building an IDE plugin that surfaces code completions, contextual code review comments, and repo-wide semantic search. Primary ask: serve long-context code reviews (multi-file, up to 600k-1M tokens) with low-latency interactive completions inside IDE.

First contact: Jordan (AE) intro email 2026-02-23. Product demo (30m) 2026-02-26 — Evan (SE) joined. Customer quote: "We need streaming completions that can handle whole PR context; chunking and KV caching are fine but want server-side cache + prefix reuse."

Trial PoC started 2026-03-03: LoopForge wired sample repo and ran 10k tokens/day for a week. Reported issues: inconsistent streaming behavior in community SDKs, unclear rate limit semantics when many devs use plugin concurrently, and cost spikes on long-history runs. They requested Node & Go SDK examples with websocket streaming and guidance on prefix/KV cache settings.

Security: asked for SOC2 attestation and if audit logs + retention controls are available (they log user prompts for troubleshooting but want retention controls). Data residency not a hard blocker — public cloud ok. They prefer SSO/SAML for admin console.

Commercial: SMB budget, expect ~5k-20k ARR first year depending on unit economics; will scale with user adoption. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions around batching/quantization to cut token costs.

Shorthand: inbound trial -> demo -> PoC running -> needs SDK + rate-limit clarity + sec docs. Good fit for hosted_api.

Stated priorities: latency first for interactive UX (~<150ms token latency target for small completions), predictable cost for long-context operations, streaming + websocket support in official SDKs, clear rate-limit/burst docs for plugin background sync.

model_preferences: Prefer open-model variants with long-context support; interested in Redwood-curated models with KV cache and prefix reuse. Will evaluate 8k/64k/1M context options depending on pricing.
latency_targets: Interactive completions: aim for <150ms per token for short completions (<=256 tokens). Accept higher for huge 100k+ context ops but want predictable tail latency.
throughput_targets: Peak expected: 30 concurrent plugin users per company instance during internal beta; baseline 5-10 reqs/sec. Looking for autoscale/burst for CI background indexing jobs.
rate_limit_expectations: Need clear RPS and burst definition; asking for per-key burst to support ~60 requests/min per dev with spiky patterns. Want guidance for token vs request quotas and how those affect plugin background sync.

bundle-size friendly browser-safe JS SDK for VSCode extension
Rust examples desirable but not blocker
notes_about_deployment_constraints: Public cloud only for now. No on-prem/VPC required. Customer values simple self-serve; may consider Dedicated if unit cost & SLAs become necessary as they scale.
poC_metrics_of_interest: average latency per token, cost per 1M tokens with long-context enabled, cache hit rate for prefix reuse, memory/kv cache overhead, streaming reconnect behavior under packet loss
